note: Simplified gyral pattern is reported in patients with homozygous and compound heterozygous missense variants, directly contradicting the proposed genotype-phenotype restriction.

evidence.text: In a cohort of twelve individuals from seven unrelated families carrying homozygous or compound heterozygous missense variants in GTF3C3, neuroimaging findings included severe cerebral and marked cerebellar atrophy with simplified gyral pattern and callosal malformations.

evidence.text: Brain imaging in four patients identified with three missense variants and one nonsense variant showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, frontal lobe hypoplasia, and moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern in one patient.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 encoding a subunit of the TFIIIC2 complex are associated with neurodevelopmental phenotypes in humans and zebrafish
source.quote: Their brain imaging showed brain atrophy with predominant cerebellar involvement, as well as hypoplasia of the frontal lobes and one patient had moderate to severe simplified gyral pattern.
